headline: 恐怖片與求生秀評論
context: 多倫多影展上，新片《River》被影評形容是「中規中矩」的生存驚悚片；同一時間，實境求生節目《Apocalypse》則被讚為「重磅大作」，設定近似末日小說情境，直接考驗參賽者末日求生的能耐。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Toronto film festival: strong performances from two experienced scream queens and some surprisingly thoughtful direction can’t elevate yet another stalk-by-numbers horror It would be unwise and unfair to expect that Toronto’s genre-led Midnight Madness strand would open with quite the same jolt as it did last year with the record-breaking horror hit Obsession . That film was an outlier in almost every respect , both as it premiered and as it was unleashed on wider crowds, the highest-grossing festival acquisition of all time topping out at over $513m worldwide and sparking genuine Oscar buzz. But it hasn’t curbed the thirst, or wider speculation, over whether anything might come even remotely close to what Curry Barker achieved and whether the festival might start to rival Sundance as the smartest place for new and exciting horror film-makers to premiere their debut projects. The jury is out with the festival having just begun, but the Midnight strand is off to a far less notable start this time around with the mostly unremarkable survival slasher River, a film directed with flashes of artfulness but written with an overwhelm of familiarity. Writer-director debuts have increasingly tended to follow that pattern (it’s OK not to do everything!) and I think Joshua Giuliano has at least shown enough visual potential here to ably steer someone else’s script to screen next time. River is premiering at the Toronto film festival and will be out in cinemas and available on Shudder in 2027 Continue reading...
sources.title: River review – so-so survival slasher offers more of the same and little else

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Geeks, toffs and biceps go to war in a wild survival experiment that answers that eternal question: if society collapsed, could you cope? This is going to be huge! Have you ever wondered how Cormac McCarthy’s wasteland novel The Road could be made into a reality show? No? Well someone who works in TV has, so here we are. Who knows if they experienced a follow-up thought: that the instinct to package the end of the world as entertainment might be the most dystopian aspect of the whole enterprise, but hey. Apocalypse (Sunday 13 September, 9pm, Channel 4) launches this week, and people are buzzing! It’s a slam dunk for a show, because we’ve all run the thought experiment. If society collapsed, how would you get food and find shelter? Would you hunker down or forge alliances? To what depravities might you stoop without the rule of law? Apocalypse puts this empty talk to the test. Seven strangers are dropped at the edge of an abandoned town. They have no access to phones, light, electricity or infrastructure. They do have access to boarded-up supermarkets, desolate buildings, broken vehicles. How soon until they eat each other? Continue reading...

thread_text:
恐怖片與求生秀評論

先看電影。多倫多影展新片《River》是一部生存驚悚片，兩位資深「尖叫女王」演出出色，但整體評價偏中規中矩，沒有太多新意。

再看電視。實境求生節目《Apocalypse》則被形容是「重磅大作」，設定類似小說《長路》的末日情境，直接考驗參賽者在文明崩潰後能否存活。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 9 月 12 日至 13 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 影劇圈今天有兩則評論，一部電影、一個節目。先說電影，多倫多影展的新片《River》是一部生存驚悚片，兩位資深演員表現不錯，但整體評價偏中規中矩。換個話題，聊聊電視——實境求生節目《Apocalypse》被形容是重磅大作，設定類似末日小說的情境，直接考驗參賽者在文明崩潰後能不能活下來。
